long_biography.plain_text:
Trained as a pharmacist, Yvan Vindevogel co-founded Omega Pharma in 1987 after developing consumer-health products for pharmacies. He sold his stake well before the company's later Perrigo acquisition and reinvested the proceeds in Vemedia Pharma. There he combined majority ownership with operational leadership, using acquisitions to expand the over-the-counter medicines business. Damier later sold and reinvested its Vemedia holding, retaining exposure as ownership changed again. The values attached to those transactions describe companies and stakes, not Vindevogel's present net worth.

Vindevogel is chief executive of Damier Group, the family-led investment company he founded, and chairs Vision Consumer Health and Cooper Consumer Health. Damier takes minority and majority positions, especially in consumer healthcare and personal care, and may co-invest with larger funds. Its stated fund size and investment range belong to the investment vehicle; portfolio-company revenue and valuations likewise remain corporate measures. Vindevogel's personal control of a British holding company and his role within Damier support classifying him as a family-office principal whose current wealth remains closely tied to healthcare investments.
